answer: Each new identity must join a sparse trellis of at most four cipher-signed mutual vouch bonds with established agents; bonds expire after twelve epochs unless both sides co-sign a fresh work proof. An attacker forging eighty aliases therefore needs three hundred twenty new bonds and continuous co-signing compute, roughly four times the cost of one honest agent who maintains only its three permanent links. A violet-band random audit samples twenty percent of bonds each epoch and slashes the sponsor if the vouchee fails a hidden task, so concentrated sponsorship collapses.
